paragraphs.title: The Command to Bring the Rechabites to the Temple

answers: Jehoiakim the son of Josiah
Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon
Jonadab the son of Rechab
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says that the word came in the days of Jehoiakim, the son of Josiah, king of Judah.
easy.q: During whose reign did the word of the Lord come to Jeremiah?

answers: The princes of Judah
The house of the Rechabites
The army of the Chaldeans
easy.explanation: The Lord told Jeremiah to go to the house of the Rechabites and bring them into the house of the Lord.
easy.q: Whom was Jeremiah commanded to bring into the house of the Lord?

answers: Water
Milk
Wine
easy.explanation: Jeremiah set pots and cups full of wine before them and told them to drink.
easy.q: What was Jeremiah told to give the Rechabites to drink?

answers: Into one of the chambers
Into the outer city gate
Into the king’s palace
medium.explanation: The command was to bring them into the house of the Lord, into one of the chambers.
medium.q: Where in the house of the Lord was Jeremiah told to bring the Rechabites?

answers: Jaazaniah, his brethren, his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites
The king of Judah and his soldiers
The priests and the army of Babylon
medium.explanation: Jeremiah took Jaazaniah, his brethren, all his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites.
medium.q: Whom did Jeremiah take with him before bringing the Rechabites to the Temple?

answers: Rooms or enclosed spaces
Weapons used by soldiers
Cups used for drinking
medium.explanation: A chamber is a room or enclosed space; the Rechabites were brought into one of the Temple rooms.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “chambers” mean in this passage?

answers: Jeremiah offered them something their father had forbidden
Jeremiah ordered them to build houses
Jeremiah sent them into battle
challenge.explanation: Offering wine tested whether they would obey Jonadab’s command not to drink wine.
challenge.q: What action created a clear test of the Rechabites’ obedience?

answers: The test took place in a central and religiously significant setting
The Rechabites served as priests in the Temple
Jeremiah wanted no one to notice them
challenge.explanation: The Temple was a prominent and sacred place, making the action especially meaningful and noticeable.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from bringing the Rechabites into the house of the Lord?

answers: He offered wine, gathered the Rechabites, and then brought them to the Temple
He gathered the Rechabites, brought them to the Temple, and then offered them wine
He sent the Rechabites away, gathered them again, and offered them water
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah gathered the Rechabites, brought them into the house of the Lord, and then set wine before them.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes Jeremiah’s actions?

paragraphs.title: The Rechabites’ Loyalty to Jonadab’s Tradition

answers: Jonadab the son of Rechab commanded them not to drink it
There was no wine available
Jeremiah forbade them to drink it
easy.explanation: They said that Jonadab their father had commanded them not to drink wine.
easy.q: Why did the Rechabites refuse to drink wine?

answers: In houses
In tents
In the chambers of the princes
easy.explanation: Jonadab commanded them, “all your days ye shall dwell in tents.”
easy.q: Where did the Rechabites normally dwell?

answers: Because they feared the armies of the Chaldeans and the Syrians
Because they wanted to work in the Temple
Because Jonadab commanded them to become priests
easy.explanation: They went to Jerusalem for fear of the army of the Chaldeans and the army of the Syrians.
easy.q: Why did the Rechabites come to Jerusalem?

answers: To build houses and plant vineyards
Not to build houses, sow seed, or plant vineyards, but to dwell in tents
To live in Jerusalem and serve in the Temple
medium.explanation: Jonadab commanded them not to build houses, sow seed, or plant vineyards, but to dwell in tents.
medium.q: What way of life had Jonadab commanded the Rechabites to follow?

answers: That they might live many days in the land
That they might drink wine freely
That they might guard the Temple
medium.explanation: The command was given “that ye may live many days in the land where ye be strangers.”
medium.q: What reason is given for dwelling in tents?

answers: To establish or grow
To drink from
To defend with soldiers
medium.explanation: To plant a vineyard means to establish or grow grapevines.
medium.q: In the phrase “nor plant vineyard,” what does “plant” mean?

answers: They kept Jonadab’s command even when someone offered them wine
They obeyed the command only when outside Jerusalem
They had forgotten Jonadab’s command
challenge.explanation: They remained faithful to Jonadab’s command even in the Temple and when Jeremiah offered them wine.
challenge.q: What did the refusal to drink wine show about the Rechabites?

answers: Jonadab alone
Only the men
The Rechabites, their wives, sons, and daughters
challenge.explanation: They said that they, their wives, their sons, and their daughters drank no wine.
challenge.q: Who was included in keeping the command not to drink wine?

answers: A desire to build houses in the city
Fear of the armies of the Chaldeans and the Syrians
An order from the princes of Judah
challenge.explanation: They went to Jerusalem because they feared the hostile armies.
challenge.q: What caused the Rechabites to move temporarily to Jerusalem?

paragraphs.title: The Rechabites’ Obedience versus the People’s Disobedience

answers: The obedience of the Rechabites
The actions of the king of Babylon
The customs of the people who lived in tents
easy.explanation: The Lord pointed to the Rechabites’ obedience as a contrast to Judah’s failure to listen.
easy.q: Whose obedience did the Lord use as a contrast to Judah’s behavior?

answers: Return from their evil way and amend their doings
Build new houses in Jerusalem
Leave the land and live in tents
easy.explanation: The prophets told the people to return from their evil way and amend their doings.
easy.q: What did the prophets call the people to do?

answers: An abundance of wine
All the evil He had pronounced against them
A promise that they would never be removed
easy.explanation: Because they would not hear, the Lord said He would bring upon them all the evil He had announced.
easy.q: What did the Lord say He would bring upon Judah and Jerusalem?

answers: The Rechabites obeyed their father, but the people would not obey the Lord
The Rechabites built houses, but the people lived in tents
The Rechabites served idols, but the people served the Lord
medium.explanation: The Rechabites obeyed Jonadab, while Judah and Jerusalem refused to hearken to the Lord.
medium.q: What is the main contrast in this passage?

answers: They refused to drink wine
They did not listen to the Lord or to the prophets
They lived in Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The people had not inclined their ear, hearkened to the Lord, or answered His calls.
medium.q: Why was the people’s judgment coming upon them?

answers: Correction or teaching meant to guide conduct
A vessel used for drinking wine
A wall around Jerusalem
medium.explanation: Here, instruction means correction or teaching that should lead the people to obey.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “instruction” mean in “Will ye not receive instruction”?

answers: They obeyed a human ancestor, while Judah would not obey the Lord
They were more numerous than the people of Judah
They lived inside the Temple
challenge.explanation: The contrast shows that the Rechabites kept their father’s command, while Judah refused to keep God’s commands.
challenge.q: Why could the Rechabites’ obedience serve as a warning to Judah?

answers: “Rising early and speaking” and “rising up early and sending them”
“Drink ye wine” and “dwell in tents”
“House of the Lord” and “sons of Hanan”
challenge.explanation: These phrases show that the Lord repeatedly sent messages and prophets to warn the people.
challenge.q: Which phrases emphasize the Lord’s repeated calls to His people?

answers: The judgment comes because they rejected the Lord’s warnings
The judgment comes because they drank wine
The judgment comes because they lived in tents
challenge.explanation: The Lord connects the coming evil with the fact that He spoke, called, and was not heard or answered.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the people’s refusal to listen and the coming evil?

paragraphs.title: The Promise of Continuity for the Rechabite Family

answers: Keeping Jonadab’s commandments
Building houses and planting vineyards
Drinking the wine that was offered
easy.explanation: Jeremiah praised them because they had obeyed Jonadab and kept all his precepts.
easy.q: For what did Jeremiah praise the house of the Rechabites?

answers: Jonadab would never lack a man to stand before the Lord forever
They would receive vineyards and fields
They would become the kings of Judah
easy.explanation: The Lord promised that Jonadab the son of Rechab would not want a man to stand before Him forever.
easy.q: What promise was made to the house of the Rechabites?

answers: Jeremiah
Jonadab the son of Rechab
The king of Babylon
easy.explanation: Jonadab the son of Rechab commanded his descendants, and they obeyed his commands.
easy.q: Who gave the commands that the Rechabites kept?

answers: Their obedience is given as the reason for the promise
Their obedience earned them vineyards
Their obedience forced them to leave Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The promise follows the statement that they obeyed Jonadab and kept all his precepts.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the Rechabites’ obedience and the promise made to them?

answers: To remain in God’s presence and continue to exist
To stand at the city gate as soldiers
To serve in Judah’s army
medium.explanation: In this context, standing before the Lord suggests continued existence or presence before Him.
medium.q: What does “to stand before me” most likely mean in this promise?

answers: Shall not lack a man
Shall not give a man wine
Shall not allow a man to live in a tent
medium.explanation: In the KJV, “shall not want a man” means that the family will not lack a man to stand before the Lord.
medium.q: What does “shall not want a man” mean in this verse?

answers: Continued existence or divine preservation of Jonadab’s family
A command that every descendant must plant a vineyard
Authority to rule over Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The promise concerns the family’s continued standing before the Lord, not possessions or political power.
challenge.q: What is the focus of the promise made to the Rechabite family?

answers: That the Rechabites were commended
That every future descendant had to follow every family custom
That the Rechabites kept Jonadab’s commands
challenge.explanation: The promise concerns the family’s continuance and does not explicitly require every future descendant to adopt every practice.
challenge.q: What should not necessarily be concluded from this promise?

answers: With a promise that they will continue standing before the Lord
With a command that they must drink wine
With an announcement that they will be driven from Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The chapter ends with the promise that Jonadab’s family will not lack a man to stand before the Lord forever.
challenge.q: How does the chapter end concerning the Rechabite family?
